messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test `testHeader()` expects the CSVPrinter to output the header row as the first row in the CSV output. The test creates a CSVPrinter using a CSVFormat configured with `.withHeader("C1", "C2", "C3")`. It then prints two records and asserts that the output string starts with the header row `C1,C2,C3\r\n`.

From the bug report, the current implementation of CSVFormat's `withHeader` method supports storing header information in the CSVFormat object, but this header functionality is only used by CSVParser and not by CSVPrinter at present. The CSVPrinter class does not automatically print the header row when printing records.

Looking at the CSVPrinter source snippets:
- `printRecord(Object...)` simply prints the values of the record.
- The `print(Object)` method prints each value but does not reference any header.
- There is no indication that CSVPrinter checks or respects the header stored in CSVFormat.
- The CSVFormat constructor stores the header internally in a private field, but the CSVPrinter does not seem to use this to output the header line.

Hence, the root cause of the test failure is that the CSVPrinter does not automatically print the header line defined in the CSVFormat passed to its constructor. It prints only the records without any header. The test expects the header to be printed, but this is not yet implemented/supported.

This is confirmed by the bug report summary stating: "CSVFormat#withHeader doesn't work with CSVPrinter" and explaining that the header option currently is only used by the CSVParser but not by CSVPrinter.

Thus, the bug arises because CSVPrinter does not handle printing the header, even if the CSVFormat contains header information.

The failing test uses CSVFormat.DEFAULT.withQuoteChar(null).withHeader(...) but CSVPrinter prints only the record lines, so the output lacks the header line, causing the assertion failure.

In summary, the missing functionality to print the header from CSVFormat in CSVPrinter causes the failure of the testHeader() test.
